title: Engineering multi-lineage inner ear organoids
text:
Inner ear disorders, such as hearing loss and dizziness, are often caused by degeneration of the sensory cells
and neurons that relay information to the brain. We have discovered a new way to produce human inner ear
cells in a culture dish. In this study, we will iteratively redesign and reformat the inner ear cells to make them
more useful for testing drug or gene therapies that could regenerate a patient’s inner ear after damage.

title: Kidney targeted AAV for gene therapy
text:
Gene delivery to the kidney has proven difficult, limiting the translation of genetic medicines to over 13% of
the global population suffering from chronic kidney disease. The current proposal focuses on studying the
biology of AAV vectors in the kidney and evolving kidney-targeted and liver de-targeted vectors for kidney
gene therapy. A specific application of this proposal involves development and optimization of gene
replacement strategies for treatment of cystinuria in relevant mouse models,

title: Core C - Virus/Vector
text:
CORE C – PROJECT NARRATIVE
The purpose of this Virus Core is to provide time and cost-efficient access to validated, high-titer stocks of the
wild-type and mutant viruses and lentiviral libraries required for the proposed studies of all six research groups
of this Program.

title: Integrated Therapies for Alcohol use in Alcohol-associated Liver Disease (ITAALD) – Mayo Clinic
text:
:
Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading cause of mortality/morbidity, and there is no FDA-approved therapy for any stage of ALD. Unfortunately, patients with ALD rarely have their underlying alcohol use disorder (AUD) concomitantly addressed. This consortium links health providers with expertise in AUD and ALD in a unified treatment strategy to evaluate novel combined treatments for AUD/ALD in patients with advanced ALD. The exiting resources of the NIAAA-funded consortium are used for patient studies, biospecimen collection and site-specific translational studies.

title: Advanced Fabrication and Integration of Nano/Pico-Electrospray Emitters in Microfluidic Systems
text:
The development of novel microfluidic system components to enhance the characterization of biomolecules is
proposed. Future microfluidic systems will aid in the determination of how biomolecules change with illness,
disease, and disease treatments. This technology will be used to improve our understanding of the mechanisms
of disease onset and progression to ultimately improve human health through early disease detection, precision
medicine, and improved treatments.

title: A functional smoothed machine learning approach for high-dimensional orofacial clefts genetic data analysis
text:
Machine learning tools have significant advantages in the risk prediction and association tests of complex
diseases for high-dimensional genetic data. The research team, led by an early-stage new investigator, will
develop a novel deep learning method using the statistical techniques in functional data analysis in hidden layers
for disease risk prediction and association testing, and will, in particular, customize the method for orofacial clefts
risks based on several large-scale databases. The results of this project will promote orofacial cleft risk prediction
and gene screening and facilitate the application of machine learning tools to high dimensional genetic data.

title: Vagus nerve stimulation to promote remyelination in multiple sclerosis
text:
Remyelination may be a powerful approach to restore lost function in patients with Multiple Sclerosis. This project
explores the ability of non-invasive, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation to repair myelin and restore
functional recovery following demyelinating injury.

title: Neuromodulation of OCD Circuitry
text: The overall goal of this project is to study three direct circuit based interventions for intractable OCD to (1) advance our understanding of the neurocircuitry of the disorder and to (2) leverage that understanding in order to develop individualized approaches to treatment that will improve safety and efficacy. Our first aim is to examine the effects of MRI guided laser thermal ventral capsulotomy in twenty patients with intractable OCD using diffusion imaging to identify cortifugal axons affected by the lesions in individuals that are related to treatment response. We will also study the effects of lesions on individual resting state and task based (PAAT) functional connectivity and their relationship to treatment outcome measures. We will utilize novel acquisition and analytic algorithms for individuals designed by Cores B and C as well as interact with Projects 1, 3 and 4 to identify false negatives and positives in the diffusion scans and to compare imaging results in patients undergoing intensive non-surgical treatments to those with lesions. The second aim is to conduct a pilot feasibility study, using a double blind crossover design, of a dual DBS implant in the vALIC and anterior cingulate bundle. The Medtronic Percept system will allow stimulation and recording of LFPs, in four patients with intractable OCD. We will stimulate and record in the vALIC and anterior cingulate, using pre-implant diffusion imaging and electric field modeling to identify which tracts are being activated. We will study the effects of stimulation at different contacts on the PAAT, and compare this to results obtained with electrophysiological recordings in the primate. Leveraging methodology developed by our collaborators (U Goodman, Dougherty) we will identify potential biomarkers of OCD provocation and treatment response. We will interact with Project 1 and 2 to compare anatomic and electrophysiological results across humans and primates as well as Cores B and C for imaging acquisition and analysis. Our third aim is to leverage ongoing studies of low intensity focused ultrasound in twenty-four patients with intractable OCD (Dougherty, Goodman PIs) and obtain pre post diffusion and task based (PAAT) functional imaging in those patients. We will compare these results to those found in lesions and DBS in the vALIC target and draw on CORE B and C as well as Project 1 and 2 to compare imaging results with nonsurgical OC subjects.

title: Transforming drug discovery research at the University of Chicago via acoustic liquid handler-Echo 650
text:
This equipment will streamline operations in the CSC and other core facilities to help researchers at the
University of Chicago discover new therapies more quickly, by providing advanced technology for rapid and
efficient drug screening. By making it easier to test thousands of potential treatments, the Echo 650 will
increase the speed and scale of our HTS screenings, supporting important research aimed at improving
therapies for cancer, infections, and other diseases, ultimately benefiting public health.

title: Neurofluid Biomarkers for Clinical Trials of Neurodegeneration
text:
A growing number of clinical trials in patients with neurodegeneration focus on the role of neurofluid (e.g.,
cerebrospinal fluid and cerebral interstitial fluid) production and clearance, and specifically, whether retention of
pathological neurotoxins that contribute to dementia sequelae are partly attributable to dysfunction of this
network. As tools for routinely characterizing this pathway in humans remain incomplete, the overall goal of this
work is to scale a deep learning architecture, developed by collaborators at Biosight LLC and Vanderbilt
University Medical Center, to create software products for characterizing the structure and function of key
elements of this pathway using routinely-acquired clinical magnetic resonance imaging scans as inputs. Once
developed, the products are intended to support clinical trials by (i) allowing for patients to be triaged for
treatments based on personalized signatures of neurofluid circulation and hypothesized predisposition to
treatment response, and (ii) providing new candidate biomarkers for emerging neurotherapeutics.

title: CT-Derived Functional Imaging for Predicting Disease Progression in COPD
text:
The proposed research will first develop the automated image processing pipeline needed to convert
inhale/exhale CT image pairs into perfusion, ventilation, and VQ functional information using state-of-the-art
deep learning methods. We will employ the functional information to develop machine learning models for
quantifying COPD severity and predicting 5-year survival. Unlike existing approaches, our novel CT-derived
functional imaging VQ markers are robust to patient breathing effort, and therefore have the potential to better
inform both clinical decision making and assessments of therapeutic efficacy.

title: SnoRNA targetome and application to cancer
text:
This proposal will develop a high throughput sequencing method that identifies cellular RNA targets of snoRNA
transcriptome-wide, and construct a comprehensive pan-cancer atlas of snoRNA targets across many types of
cancer cells for studying the role of snoRNAs in cancer biology.

title: Establishing orbital and cranial vessel wall MRI enhancement as an imaging biomarker in giant cell arteritis
text:
Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is a systemic vasculitis complicated by significant treatment- and disease-related
disability, including blindness. This study will evaluate the use of magnetic resonance imaging to detect vascular
inflammation in the blood vessels of the head and eyes in GCA. An imaging test that detects disease flares and
eye involvement can lead to personalized treatment strategies, resulting in better quality of life, fewer treatment
side effects, and lower rates of disability (including blindness).

title: Training Program in Psychiatric Genetics and Translational Research
text: Scientific advances in genetics require sophisticated and innovative approaches, particularly when applied to the complex biology of psychiatric disorders. To reduce the burden of mental illness, clinical research must translate discoveries from genetics and neuroscience into effective strategies for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment that improve health outcomes across populations. Integrating these advances within a unified, evidence-based framework will strengthen the impact of psychiatric research and enhance public health.

title: Fractional flow reserve versus Angiography for Multivessel Evaluation (FAME) 3 Extended
text:
Coronary artery disease, or narrowing of the blood vessels that provide blood to the heart, is the most common
cause of death in the United States and can be treated with either coronary bypass surgery or coronary stent
placement. This study will evaluate outcomes, including death and quality of life, at 10 years in 1,500 patients
with coronary disease who have already been randomized to either bypass surgery or stenting. If outcomes
with stenting are equivalent to bypass surgery, it will provide millions of patients with a less invasive option for
treatment of their coronary disease.

title: Training Program on Genetic Variation and Human Phenotypes
text:
Our training program in human genetics offers pre-doctoral students the opportunity to
learn and apply human genetics science in a highly collaborative and collegial environment rich in
resources that can stimulate human genetics research. BioVU, the biobank at Vanderbilt University, for
example, has more than 250,000 subjects and past human genetics students have been unusually
productive because of the opportunities in conducting human genetic studies in these data. Our
students receive a broad-based education and have traditionally pursued a wide range of research in
human genetics and professional careers.

title: Aging, DNA methylation, and incident cardiovascular disease in breast cancer survivors
text:
Breast cancer survivors are a growing segment of the population who experience higher rates of
cardiovascular disease (CVD) incidence and mortality than women without breast cancer. Biological aging
metrics derived from blood DNA methylation data are associated with both breast cancer and CVD incidence,
making them an attractive solution for improving our understanding of CVD etiology and enhancing risk
stratification of breast cancer patients. Findings from this proposal can improve breast cancer outcomes by
providing vital information at cancer diagnosis that guides cardiac surveillance and cancer treatment decisions.

title: Investigating stem and progenitor cell quality assurance in development andregeneration.
text:
Macrophages are a highly dynamic population which interact with stem and progenitor cells across many
tissues in development, disease, and regeneration. These interactions can selectively amplify or eliminate
specific stem/progenitor cells and shape tissue growth and architecture. We will explore the stimuli which
trigger macrophage interactions, the mechanisms which determine the nature of these interactions, and the
consequences of these interactions across multiple developmental and regenerative contexts to develop an
integrated research program that explores questions of immune mediated stem/progenitor cell regulation.

title: Machine learning methods for identifying person-level mechanisms of alcohol use among sexual and gender minority intersections
text:
Alcohol use among sexual and gender minorities is a significant public health concern, yet individual
differences and processes of risk among these communities remain unclear. In this proposal, we aim to identify
intersectional, systemic, and minority stress factors driving of alcohol risk in these communities using novel
machine learning methods in longitudinal national data preceding, during, and after the coronavirus pandemic.
This will identify for whom and why alcohol risk is greatest among these underserved populations, informing
specialized strategies for alcohol prevention and responsive public health intervention during future global health
crises.

title: Pathways and Regulators Driving Progressive Islet Cell Dysfunction in Type 1 Diabetes
text:
Type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains a devastating disease, and the molecular mechanisms driving its onset and
progression are still poorly understood. Herein, we aim to identify novel in situ pathways and molecular
regulators that drive early T1D progression by applying spatial proteomics and lipidomics profiling of human
islet microenvironments in patient pancreatic tissue. Newly discovered mediators from this high-dimensional
dataset will be further assessed for their functional roles and translational potential as therapeutic targets.
